parts.t: English Bluff rises above the north end of Tsawwassen Beach, next to the ferry terminal causeway. It has a lookout park and a school. On a bluff, slope and drainage matter.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 11, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Delta.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

parts.t: Delta adopted a new Official Community Plan in 2024. Zoning and the plan designation apply lot by lot.
Delta now allows 3 units on a single detached or duplex lot up to 280 square metres and 4 units on a bigger lot. Secondary, coach and garden suites count toward those limits.

blocks.text: Before you buy in English Bluff

parts.t: Ask the City of Delta what the property is zoned and what the plan says about it and the lots around it.
Use the Delta School District school locator for the exact address.
Get a slope and drainage check.
On a bluff lot, have a professional look at retaining walls, slope drainage and any geotechnical report.
Ask whether it was permitted before you count on it.
Ask whether any covenant protects the view, and what the lots below could build under their zoning.
Look for covenants on slope, drainage or building height, and for any right of way to the beach stairs.
Send me your address and I’ll give you a call to talk about how to get the most value from your home.

Is there an official English Bluff boundary?
English Bluff is an MLS® sub-area name used by the real estate board rather than an official municipal boundary, so ask me to verify any specific address.
A park at 253 English Bluff Road with a lookout over the Gulf Islands, a stairway down to Tsawwassen Beach, picnic tables and trails.

Is English Bluff close to the ferry?
The bluff is next to the ferry terminal causeway. The terminal is at 1 Ferry Causeway, and TransLink route 620 runs from it to Bridgeport Station.
